sections.content: How many people stayed in East Grinstead after gaining qualifications?

East Grinstead is a medium-sized town in the South East. East Grinstead does not have its own university.

East Grinstead has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, East Grinstead ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,300 state-school pupils from East Grinstead who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 485 (37%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 415 (32%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare East Grinstead to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of East Grinstead's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in East Grinstead in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left East Grinstead move to?

Of East Grinstead's graduates, 210 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those graduates (17%) were living fairly locally, in the Crawley travel to work area (TTWA).

Of East Grinstead's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 115 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 50 of those qualified non-graduates (43%) were living fairly locally, in the Crawley travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in East Grinstead's GCSE cohort:

  • 125 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 35 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 23% of graduates and 25% of qualified non-graduates living in East Grinstead had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 350 graduates and 395 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in East Grinstead. This is compared with the 485 graduates and 415 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 77% of the graduates had also lived in East Grinstead as GCSE pupils, while 23% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in East Grinstead in 2018 to 2019, 75% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 25% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
